D	387	`core/sort` takes a comparison with a context	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d387-core-sort-takes-a-comparison-with-a-context	Chosen: `sort.sort_by(values, by, less)` sorts with `less: (by: context, left: item, right: item) -> (yes: bool)`, generic over `item` and `context`, and passes `by` to every comparison unchanged. A context is any value: a slice of the shared storage, a record holding one, or a pointer through which the comparison counts or caches. It is the same heapsort as `sort`, with no allocation, constant storage and bounded depth, and the comparison must be a strict weak ordering while it runs. A context whose type disagrees with the comparison's is D138's L0340. `sort` and `sort_selection` are unchanged, so no image that sorts by evidence grows.
D	388	A library failure atom has words for a person	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d388-a-library-failure-atom-has-words-for-a-person	Chosen: `core/failure` is a shared freestanding module of one type and one routine. `failure.reason` is the union of every atom a `core` module fails with, thirty-nine of them since D1276 from `core/mem`, `core/map`, `core/tree`, `core/io`, `core/net`, `core/text`, `core/cache` and `core/line`, and `failure.words(problem)` returns a fixed phrase for each: lower case with no final stop, so that it reads after a subject and a colon, static text that borrows nothing, the same on every target and in every locale. D	405	One match arm names several cases, and none of them binds	Decisions: Structs, variants and nesting	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d405-one-match-arm-names-several-cases-and-none-of-them-binds	Chosen: `match_arm ::= match_label ("," match_label)+ ":" ...` beside the one-case arm: an arm may name several cases of an atom set, a variant part or a pointer union, separated by commas, and what it runs is shared. It means the empty bound block: the call's effects up to its failure stay, and the next statement runs. D	410	A byte-packed C record has fields with no address of their own	Decisions: Declared types, ranges and layout	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d410-a-byte-packed-c-record-has-fields-with-no-address-of-their-own	Chosen: `layout(c, packed)` is a C record laid out as C's packed attribute lays one out: its fields in written order, each at alignment one, with no padding, so its size is the sum of its fields' sizes and its alignment is one. Its placement asks no C ABI for an alignment, so it stands on every target, Cortex-M0 included, where `layout(c)` does not. D228's rule for a packed image's fields carries over, which answers D239's objection: a field, at any depth, has no address of its own. `addr`, an `inout` argument and a slice of anything inside the record are L0336, and the whole record is what a pointer reaches. Fields are read and written by copy. Everything the record holds by value besides a scalar or pointer is itself of alignment one — an array of `u8`, `i8`, `bool` or packed records, or a nested `layout(c, packed)` record — because a whole array or record is copied and passed as a value, and only a scalar is assembled where it lies; anything else is L0346 at the field. Another C record or an ordinary struct may hold a packed record as a field.\n\nA scalar inside a packed record may sit at any address. On x86-64 and arm64, Linux, Darwin and FreeBSD alike, an ordinary load or store does not need alignment and the backends emit one. RV64 and Cortex-M0 move such a scalar one byte at a time, least significant first: ARMv6-M faults on every unaligned halfword or word access, and a misaligned RISC-V access may trap or be emulated by the kernel. Lowering marks an address slot that reaches such a scalar, so an access through a computed element address is moved the same way. `layout(c, optimal)` and any second word but `packed` after `c` are L0103.
D	411	`offsetof t.field` measures where a field begins	Decisions: Structs, variants and nesting	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d411-offsetof-t-field-measures-where-a-field-begins	Chosen: `offsetof t.field` is a `usize`, the byte offset at which `field` of the struct type `t` begins in the selected target's layout. The selection may continue through nested struct fields, `offsetof frame.head.id`, and `t` may be named through its module. The word is contextual like `lenof`: only a name followed by a dotted name makes the measurement, so `offsetof(x)` still calls a routine of that name. The checker finds the prefix resolution bound to a type and holds every selection after it to a field; a missing field is L0308, and a scalar type, a path through an array element or a variant case, a variant part itself and a `layout(packed)` image's bit field, which has no byte offset, are L0304. A `layout(c, packed)` record's field has an offset like any other. Like D44's measurements the IR carries the question, not the answer: a `Measure_Offset` carries the record's field run, its layout policy and the path's source positions, and the backend answers it from the target's placement. The checker's module fold reads the same placement, so the measurement may stand in a module value and, by D412, in an assertion.
D	412	A compiler assertion measures a declared type's layout	Decisions: Modules and compile time	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d412-a-compiler-assertion-measures-a-declared-type-s-layout	Chosen: `sizeof` and `alignof` of any type and D411's `offsetof` stand in a `compiler.assert`. Configuration still validates such an assertion when it selects arms, but folds it only after checking has laid out the declared types it measures: resolution resolves the measured types and paths, the checker checks them as it checks any measurement, and the same closed fold then reads their sizes, alignments and offsets from the checked target layout beside the options and compiler facts it always read. This is measurement, not compile-time execution: no user routine runs, and the checker already computes target-aware layout (D44). A fixed condition and an option default still measure scalar types only, because a declared type's layout depends on the arms they select; a declared type there is L0305 with a note that says so.
D	413	A C record's last zero-length array is its flexible array member	Decisions: Declared types, ranges and layout	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d413-a-c-record-s-last-zero-length-array-is-its-flexible-array-member	Chosen: the last field of a `layout(c)` or `layout(c, packed)` record may be `[0]T` of a C element, and it is the record's flexible array member. As C gives the member its element's alignment, it takes `T`'s alignment there, so the record's offset of it and its padded size are C's: `struct linux_dirent64` measures 24 with its name at 19. D136's zero-element shape keeps alignment one everywhere else. As in C, at least one field precedes it. The record's trailing elements are not storage the record owns: a program reaches them as a slice of the buffer the record was written into, at `offsetof record.member` (D411), which keeps that buffer's origin. Because those elements would overlap whatever follows the record, a record that ends in one is refused as an array element (L0304) and as a field of a C record (L0346), and a C signature takes it only by pointer (D414). A zero-length array before the last field is L0346 at that field.

A pointer to either is an ordinary C pointer, and C reads and writes the record through it with the layout D410 and D413 give it.
D	415	`public` is not an export: only what is named for the linker is global	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d415-public-is-not-an-export-only-what-is-named-for-the-linker-is-global	Chosen: [1975]'s list is the whole of a program's global symbols: the hosted or firmware entry, C imports and public C definitions under their declared spelling, every routine and datum with a link name whether public or not, every public definition in a machine convention, and every Cortex-M placement. Every other routine and datum is a local symbol under its own name, on every backend: x86-64, arm64 and RV64 ELF, Darwin's Mach-O and Cortex-M0. A collision with the C library or a linked object cannot happen, so none is detected, and the debugger, a backtrace and `nm` keep the source name. An export is what something outside the program can call, so it, and not a public routine, is what D296 roots and what marks a routine's address exposed; a public routine the program alone calls may be folded with another of the same code or specialized like a private one.
D	416	A datum takes a link name on a hosted target	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d416-a-datum-takes-a-link-name-on-a-hosted-target	Chosen: a module datum takes `link(symbol: ...)` on every target, which makes it a global symbol under that name (D415) whether it is public or not. On a hosted target the name has [1975]'s external shape, as a routine's has, is never `main`, the hosted entry's, and like every link name is distinct from every other explicit one; L0347 refuses anything else and says so. Cortex-M data keep [1640]'s identifier shape and reserved prefixes.
D	417	Two items of one spelling: the one that is not an export takes its module's path	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d417-two-items-of-one-spelling-the-one-that-is-not-an-export-takes-its-module-s-path	Chosen: an item that is not an export and whose spelling another item of the program holds takes its module's logical path with every `/` as `.`, or `main` for the entry module, then `.` and its name: `core.arena.reset`, `main.read`. An identifier holds no `.`, so only an explicit link name can hold that too; then, and for every instance of one generic routine after the first, the item takes the first free of `.1`, `.2` and so on after it, in item order. The qualified spelling depends on the declaration alone, never on what else the program contains; whether an item needs it, and an instance's number, do. An export never yields.
D	418	The POSIX and Linux layers keep their routines' own names	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d418-the-posix-and-linux-layers-keep-their-routines-own-names	Chosen: under D415 a public routine is a local symbol, so it can replace nothing, and the prefixes are dropped: 174 link names go, and each routine keeps its own name, which a debugger and a backtrace now show. No C peer, C runtime or assembly block called any of them by a prefixed name. The two symbols the C runtime and the kernel do reach keep theirs: the process entry `_landin_start` and `_landin_host_initialize_arguments`, which a C-owned `main` calls. `_landin_start_main` stays a public C definition, which `_landin_start` calls from its assembly block.
D	419	A parameter whose type names no generic formal is an ordinary context	Decisions: Concepts, generics and runtime dispatch	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d419-a-parameter-whose-type-names-no-generic-formal-is-an-ordinary-context	Chosen: a runtime parameter of a generic routine whose written type names no formal of the routine, other than formals an explicit static list already fixed, is an ordinary context, as [1880] defines one. An argument that needs a context and fills one, an array literal or repetition, `ptr(integer)`, `any(pointer)`, a struct literal or construction, or `zeroed`, takes no part in deduction and contributes no equation: the instance's ordinary call check types it against the concrete parameter, exactly as a non-generic call does. An array literal for a closed slice parameter `[]E` is therefore lent on D309's terms: each element is checked against E, so `any(addr x)` takes its concept from `[]any C`; it is formed in written order in the caller's frame, lent read-only with frame origin, so a result `from` that parameter cannot leave the caller; `[]mut E` and `utf8` still take none. A parameter whose type names an open formal keeps D138's context-free deduction, and `pick([1, 2])` against `values: []item` is still L0304: its refusal now names the binding that gives the literal a type, `values := [...]` when no element needs a context and `values: [N]E = [...]`, with the count written, when one does. An `any(pointer)` with more than one exact concept, L0342, names the pointee and every concept it conforms to, so the `any C` to write is one of them.
D	420	A named construction carries its type into deduction	Decisions: Concepts, generics and runtime dispatch	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d420-a-named-construction-carries-its-type-into-deduction	Chosen: a named construction is self-typed. In a generic call its written type's body is the descriptor deduction matches with the parameter's pattern, binding a formal there as a struct place would, and the instance's ordinary call check then builds it in the caller's frame as it builds any struct argument. An untyped struct literal `(f: ...)` still needs a context: D419 gives it a closed parameter's, and a parameter whose type is a formal gives it none.
D	421	A generic instance is a symbol named after its routine	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d421-a-generic-instance-is-a-symbol-named-after-its-routine	Chosen: an instance's symbol is spelled from the generic routine it was made from, and an evidence provider's from the routine whose evidence it binds. D	422	A library file is recorded under `/landin-library/`	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d422-a-library-file-is-recorded-under-landin-library	Chosen: a file of a `core`, `hosted` or `platform` module is recorded in DWARF's file table and the source map as `/landin-library/`, its module path and its own name: `/landin-library/core/vec/vec.ldn`, the name D361's report gives it behind one fixed prefix. D	424	An `if` inside a line is laid out from its `if`	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d424-an-if-inside-a-line-is-laid-out-from-its-if	Chosen: an `if` that begins inside a line is laid out from its `if`: a `then` that begins a line, each `elsif` and `else` and its `end if` stand under the `if`, and each arm's body four columns in from it. The table D252 measured is the case of it whose arms each fit one line. An `if` that begins its line is laid out as before.
D	425	A list of bytes is the growable byte container	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d425-a-list-of-bytes-is-the-growable-byte-container	Chosen: `vec.list(u8)` is the growable byte container, with three operations over it. `vec.append_bytes` copies a slice after the bytes the list holds; `vec.spare_bytes` lends the spare capacity past them, at least the bytes asked for, as the buffer a read fills; and `vec.extend_bytes` counts the bytes written there as appended. The first two grow the list as `push` does, doubling, or to exactly what is asked when doubling is not enough, and report `mem.out_of_memory` changing nothing; counting more than the spare capacity is `mem.out_of_bounds`, also changing nothing. Beneath them `core/mem` gives the byte storage the same three: `spare_bytes`, `admit_bytes` and `admit_copy`, the last failing with `full`. The spare capacity holds whatever the backing held, which every byte value is, so the view is only for bytes: a spare slot of another item type could hold no value of it, an atom set's among them. The copy is `mem.copy`, a word at a time where it moves words and a byte at a time on firmware, and so is the move when the list grows: `mem.transfer_prefix`, which `mem.reserve_storage` moves a block's items with when the provider cannot grow it in place, copies their bytes whole rather than a typed transfer per item, and D356's protocol, a growth asked in place before an allocation, stays as it was. Reading reverse-complement's input on Linux x86-64 at `--optimize speed` into a list through `spare_bytes` takes 0.40 seconds, and 0.44 through `append_bytes` from a 64 KiB buffer, against 2.5 to 3.7 with the reserve moving items one at a time and 0.23 through `core/text`'s growing builder, whose `resize` lets `hosted/heap` move a large block's pages rather than copy them. Reverse-complement keeps the builder: through a list it took 0.94 seconds against the builder's 0.79.
D	426	The binding generator writes packed and flexible-member records, and types their pointers	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d426-the-binding-generator-writes-packed-and-flexible-member-records-and-types-their-pointers	Chosen: a struct carrying its own `__attribute__((packed))`, with every field of alignment one as D410 requires, is written `layout(c, packed)`, and a struct whose last field, after at least one other, is `T name[]` or GNU's `T name[0]` is written with a last `[0]T` field, its member at its element's alignment, or at one inside a packed record. `#pragma pack`, `packed` on a single member, `aligned` beside `packed`, a packed field of alignment above one under the `native` policy and a flexible member elsewhere or alone stay refused, each naming the decision it would break; `auto` keeps a packed record that breaks D410 C-owned and opaque, and a flexible-member record has no opaque form. Where the header passes either by value, D414 decides: an imported function gets a generated wrapper taking and returning it through `ptr record` or `ptr mut record`, a global gets typed address, read and write adapters, and an opaque record's field gets accessors through typed pointers; an export, a callback or an incoming-varargs handler carrying one by value is refused. A pointer to a selected packed or flexible-member record is `ptr [mut] record`, so its fields are reached without a cast; a pointer to any other record stays `ptr u8`, so no binding generated before changes. `bindings.json` records `packed`, `flexible_member` and `pointer_only` for every native record.
D	427	A distinct type has its base's equality, and flags update in place	Decisions: Declared types, ranges and layout	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d427-a-distinct-type-has-its-base-s-equality-and-flags-update-in-place	Chosen: `==` and `<>` take two values of one distinct type whose base has equality: a scalar, an atom or atom set, a pointer or a function value. The answer is the base's own comparison of the two representations; a pointer union, which has no equality (D189, D429), stays without one when it is a distinct base. Ordering stays a scalar base's. Over an unsigned integer base, `x &= y`, `x ^= y` and `x |= y` mean `x = x op y` with the place `x` reached once, its index and any call in it evaluated once, as every updating assignment's place is [0390]; the target must already be assigned, because the operator reads it. A distinct type whose base has no equality, a struct, an array, a slice or a pointer union, is refused as that, "a distinct type whose base has no equality", rather than as a struct.\n\nThe comparison reads the one representation child as the base's carrier: an atom's code, a pointer's or function's address. No origin is created or consumed, the result is `bool`, and the representation is unchanged, so no backend or layout moves.
D	428	A distinct type has a zero image when its base has one	Decisions: Declared types, ranges and layout	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d428-a-distinct-type-has-a-zero-image-when-its-base-has-one	Chosen: a distinct type has a zero image exactly when its base has one, because its representation is its base's, and it is then in `zeroable`'s compiler family. A record, an array or a variant payload holding one is zeroed as it would be holding the base, in a body and in module data, whose image is all zeros. The word `zeroed` written for the distinct type itself is refused, L0328 with the route `name(0)`: an identity has no obvious reading of zero, which is [0540]'s second property. Inside a generic routine's instance whose type actual is the distinct type, `zeroed` for the formal is the image `zeroable` promised and is accepted. L0328's note now names a distinct type over a type without a zero image among the causes.
D	429	A pointer union compares with one of its own atoms	Decisions: Pointers and raw storage	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d429-a-pointer-union-compares-with-one-of-its-own-atoms	Chosen: `u == a` and `u <> a`, where `u` is a pointer union of one atom or of several and `a` is an atom value whose atoms all belong to `u`'s set, answer whether `u` holds that atom, with the atom on either side. No address is read and none can be obtained: the pointer still comes out only through a `ptr` arm. A one-atom union holds its atom exactly when its carrier is zero; a union of several atoms holds one exactly when its code cell holds that atom's code, which is zero for the pointer case (D235). Both operands are evaluated, left first. Comparing two unions, or a union with a pointer, stays L0335, and its note now names both routes, the atom test and `match` with `ptr (p):`.
D	430	An assignment on every edge that leaves a loop holds after it	Decisions: Control flow	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d430-an-assignment-on-every-edge-that-leaves-a-loop-holds-after-it	Chosen: the checker iterates a loop's head to its fixed point, so the state after the loop is the join of the edges that actually leave it, each taken from the converged head: a `while`'s false test and a `for`'s exhaustion, through `complete` when there is one, and every `break` with the cleanups it runs. A name assigned on every one of them is assigned after the loop, a named return as well as a local. This is sound for zero iterations because the false-test edge carries only the facts the head had before any body ran. Consumption (D223) was already the join of the actual exits. The IR verifier's own slot walk is path-based and needed no change. Where a path does leave a name unassigned, L0302 now says that a path that arrives has not assigned it, rather than that none did.
D	431	A final control whose only answers diverge is a statement	Decisions: Control flow	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d431-a-final-control-whose-only-answers-diverge-is-a-statement	Chosen: a routine's final `if` or `match` whose every answer is a call that does not return, or a nested `if` or `match` of the same kind, answers nothing, and the checker takes it as the statement it then is: its arms are checked as statements, and each arm that falls through must have assigned the named returns, as after any statement. The parser cannot know this, since `noreturn` is a signature's, so the checker decides it. A final control with one real answer stays a value, its diverging arms needing no value [1560].

D	437	A module value reads a compiler fact	Decisions: Modules and compile time	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d437-a-module-value-reads-a-compiler-fact	Chosen: a module value's image may read a compiler fact, and reads the value the configuration stage found once it selected the arms. D	439	A system's own module is empty elsewhere, not conditionally imported	Decisions: Modules and compile time	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d439-a-system-s-own-module-is-empty-elsewhere-not-conditionally-imported	Chosen: that shape is the way. A system's own module is imported unconditionally and declares its routines inside its own `fixed if`; on another system it declares nothing, and a call to one of them there is L0201 saying the module declares it only for another target: a call this system does not have, not a misspelling, which a misspelling's near names would suggest. D	440	An untracked step re-enters tracking through a written contract	Decisions: Lifetime, escape and allocation	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d440-an-untracked-step-re-enters-tracking-through-a-written-contract	Chosen: no new conversion. Origin and permission end at an integer step and the compiler does not recover them; what a caller is checked against is the routine's signature. A routine that indexes a raw table writes its result `from` the table, as `platform/posix`'s `argument` writes `from table`; a routine around an assembly block takes the storage as `ptr mut u8` or `[]mut u8`, as `platform/linux`'s `read` does. Callers are then held to that `from`, mutability and `escaping` as to any other signature's, and an immutable buffer is refused at the call. The routine's own body is not checked against them: an integer-made pointer satisfies any `from` clause [0470], so the written contract is the routine author's claim, the unsafe backing obligation [1720] already gives allocator internals. Such a routine is kept small, and private where it can be, so that the claim has one author. This is a deliberate non-guarantee, not a gap a later check is expected to close. L0330's note for a pointer operand names the typed parameter.\n\nA C table whose extent the program knows from C, an `argv` beside its `argc`, may keep its origin instead: type the pointer `ptr [1]t`, take `p.val[0..<1]` and widen that slice inside `unchecked` to the extent C gives. The slice derives from `p`, so indexing and returning it are tracked and a missing `from` is L0316. The widening is the program's claim about the extent and stays inside `unchecked`, as [0510]'s narrow extension and `core/mem`'s `block_bytes` do. It is sanctioned only over storage that holds initialised `t`s, which a table C filled does; it is not [0510]'s `slice_from`, whose fault is a typed view over storage that holds no `t`.\n\nA concept entry whose result has no `from`, as `mem.allocator`'s `resize` declares, returns the block it was given as `ptr(usize(block))`: an allocation borrows nothing, and [0810]'s conversion says so. Returning `block` itself is L0316, since the result would derive from a parameter the clause does not name, and writing `from block` is L0316 too, on the edge that returns a fresh allocation (D222). L0316's explanation names this route.
D	441	`escaping` stays part of C-symbol compatibility	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d441-escaping-stays-part-of-c-symbol-compatibility	Chosen: the comparison keeps `escaping`. A Landin caller of the import is checked against what the import says, so an import without `escaping` would let a caller pass `addr local` to a definition that keeps the pointer, a frame escape no check sees [0780]. When two declarations of one symbol differ in nothing but `escaping`, L0347 says so, names the parameter and says to repeat it on both.
