D	1034	Prototype 5's firmware counterpart, and where it departs from the sketch	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1034-prototype-5-s-firmware-counterpart-and-where-it-departs-from-the-sketch	Chosen: `compiler/tests/counterpart` has the sketch's three modules, `firmware/serial` and `firmware/trace`, and shares the hosted server's `app/protocol` unchanged and prototype 1's derived receive driver. The board is one handle providing `fibre.scheduler`, `fibre.turns` and `time.clock`: its turns are `core/fibre/stacks`' round, held as `any fibre.turns`, with the application's idler waiting for an interrupt, and its sleep yields until the tick count, widened to 64 bits, has moved by the span's whole ticks and one more, so it never returns early. SysTick counts a millisecond a tick through `atomic.sole_add` (D449). The taker reads whatever has arrived at each turn through `uart.read` and yields when nothing has, since prototype 1's DMA notifies only at the half and the end of its ring. `firmware/serial` is the transmit side, an `io.writer` over the UART's data register, in a module of its own so prototype 1's derivative is unchanged. A line that is no request, or one longer than the queue's 64 bytes, is answered `malformed` through `protocol.refuse`, as the hosted session answers it; a line arriving with four waiting is refused `busy`; every line is numbered as it arrives. Each fibre's stack is 2,048 bytes.
D	1035	The counterpart's trace, and what its oracle requires	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1035-the-counterpart-s-trace-and-what-its-oracle-requires	Chosen: the firmware records, in `firmware/trace`, each line's arrival as `received` or `refused`, numbered in arrival order, and each request's `started` when it leaves the queue and `finished` when its answer is flushed, each with the tick it happened at; a trace that would overflow is marked lost. The lane feeds `WAIT 200 a`, then `NOW b` once `a` has begun, so the request for two in flight is presented as the hosted client presents it, and in two more scenarios a full queue and lines that are no request. The oracle, `judge` in `environments/cortex-m/counterpart.py`, derives each line's answer from the protocol's rules written again in Python and fails a run on a missing answer; an answer begun while another was being answered, or out of arrival order; a wait answered in fewer ticks than it asked; `busy` with room in the queue, or a fifth request queued; a byte the device did not take; a lost trace; a second request that did not arrive while the first was being answered; and a trap, a halt or a timeout. Four controls build the same source with one mutation each, two answerers, a dropped answer, a take past the queue and a SysTick never started, and each must fail for its own reason. A tick is a millisecond of the emulator's clock, which under the harness's instruction counting reaches the next tick across each stop at an access to the synthetic device, so the ticks order events and bound waits from below and are no measure of the firmware's own time.
D	1036	The counterpart runs on a description of the micro:bit's own chip	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1036-the-counterpart-runs-on-a-description-of-the-micro-bit-s-own-chip	Chosen: the lane compiles the counterpart with `environments/cortex-m/lanes/lane-microbit.ldn`, which imports a lane description of QEMU's micro:bit, the nRF51822 the Cortex-M0 lanes run on: 256 KiB of flash at zero, and the reference's 16 KiB of RAM with its 4 KiB stack at 0x2000_0000. `descriptions.json` records it as it records the other lane descriptions, and the lane holds every image to it. D	1042	A source D290 asks nothing of lends a call's result no view	Decisions: Lifetime, escape and allocation	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1042-a-source-d290-asks-nothing-of-lends-a-call-s-result-no-view	Chosen: at a call that reaches a generic instance, a `from` source whose parameter is written with a type formal, is not `inout`, and whose instance type holds no reference supplies the result no origin: the result neither derives from the argument nor locks it, or the place it was copied from, against `inout` and `sink`, and a result whose every source is of this kind is as independent as one that names none. The instance's body can return nothing derived from such an argument (D290), and a value parameter's own storage is the callee's frame, which no result may view. An `inout` source lends its storage whatever its type holds, so it keeps the lock, and an instance type that holds a reference binds as written.
D	1045	A write to a blocking descriptor takes no more than a pipe reported ready takes whole	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1045-a-write-to-a-blocking-descriptor-takes-no-more-than-a-pipe-reported-ready-takes-whole	Chosen: for a write of more than `PIPE_BUF` bytes, `posix.pipe_atomic`, 4096 on Linux and 512 on Darwin and FreeBSD, the provider reads the descriptor's mode and kind: a non-blocking one, whose write fails EAGAIN rather than wait, and a regular file, which never waits for a reader, are handed all of it, and any other is handed `PIPE_BUF` bytes a call once it is ready. A blocking write of no more than `PIPE_BUF` bytes to a pipe waits only until all of it fits, and a pipe reported ready has that room: Linux's `poll` and epoll report a pipe writable when one of its buffers is free, and a buffer is a page, never smaller than 4096 bytes; Darwin's and FreeBSD's `poll` and kqueue's write filter report it when at least `PIPE_BUF` bytes are free. No manual page promises that threshold: Linux's `poll(2)` says only that a write larger than the room still blocks, and `kqueue(2)` that the filter's data is the room left. The claim rests on the kernels' pipe code and on the regression fixture below, which every hosted target runs. A shorter write asks the system nothing more, and a longer one asks once, not per piece. Another writer, a thread or a process, can still fill the room between the report and the write; a terminal or a blocking socket the program hands the provider may report room for less than `PIPE_BUF`, and a write to one can still hold the thread until its other end reads. A child's pipe the system leaves blocking stays as it is rather than fail the spawn, since the cap covers it and the child has already started. One report wakes every fibre that waits on the descriptor, and the first to run can fill the room or take the input again, so a woken fibre asks the descriptor once more before its call and waits again when it is no longer ready; a read on a blocking descriptor is held to the same.
D	1046	A signal ends a command with one report and status, at once unless it holds something to recover	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1046-a-signal-ends-a-command-with-one-report-and-status-at-once-unless-it-holds-something-to-recover	Chosen: an interrupt, termination or hangup always ends a command the same way: its last line is `refine: cancelled by signal N` and its exit status is 128 plus the number, whether or not it held anything, so a script reads one outcome. When the command holds nothing a signal could leave half done, the handler does both itself, there and then, with `write` and `_exit` alone: a long `refine check` stops within the moment the signal takes to arrive, and says nothing else. Something is held from before it exists until it is gone: an open publication and its workspace, a private directory, a tool's capture and the unreaped tool, and the rewrite of a source `refine fmt` is replacing; reading, parsing, checking and lowering hold nothing. While something is held the signal is recorded as before, and the command answers it where one stage hands over to the next: between the frontend's stages, when the outputs are reserved, after the optimizer and after emission, as well as in the tool supervisor and every publication step; `refine fmt` stops before its next source. A stage is never interrupted, so what is recovered is whole. A recorded signal that is not answered within ten seconds ends the process by that signal, as `SIGKILL` would, with no last line, leaving the workspace its destination records describe: a stage that never reaches a boundary cannot hold the process, and ten seconds is longer than stopping a tool and putting the outputs back takes. A caller that started refine with `SIGALRM` ignored has no such limit. The closed-pipe signal is D1047's and keeps its quiet end.
D	1047	The file-size and closed-pipe signals reach the recovery written for their errors	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1047-the-file-size-and-closed-pipe-signals-reach-the-recovery-written-for-their-errors	Chosen: refine ignores `SIGXFSZ` for the length of a command, so the write fails with the error and the recovery written for it runs; a tool and the program `refine run` starts are given the inherited disposition back. `SIGPIPE` is one of the signals D1046 records: with nothing held it ends the process by its default action, as before and without D1046's line, and while a run's directory exists the write fails instead, the directory is removed, and refine exits with 128 plus the signal's number.

D	1060	An assembly input's file directives are found wherever the word stands	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1060-an-assembly-input-s-file-directives-are-found-wherever-the-word-stands	Chosen: the scan decides nothing an assembler might read otherwise. It skips only what every assembler the targets link with skips: a `/* */` comment, a double-quoted string with its backslash escapes, which the scan ends at the end of its line at the latest, and the character after a `'`. Everywhere else the word `.include` or `.incbin`, in either case and not continuing a symbol, is the directive: behind a label or a separator, and also behind what one target reads as a comment marker. It names its file plainly, a double-quoted absolute path without a backslash on the same line, or the input is refused as L0003. An input that uses `.macro`, `.irp`, `.irpc` or `.altmacro` is refused, since a macro can form the word from its arguments where no scan finds it. An assembly input is text whatever bytes it holds. The assembly the compiler emits holds no file directive at all, and one found there is refused: no backend writes one and [1990] keeps directives out of block text. A linker script keeps its own tokens, where `#` and `/* */` are comments to the linker as they are to the scan.\n\nThis refuses inputs that were accepted: an assembly operand that defines a macro, and one that mentions a file directive in a line comment.
D	1061	A standard output that cannot be written is the host's failure	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1061-a-standard-output-that-cannot-be-written-is-the-host-s-failure	Chosen: a command's output is written and flushed where the failure can be told, and a failure is reported on standard error as "refine: cannot write to standard output" with status 71, the status of a host that failed the compiler, which the language server's channel already uses. What the command reported is still written to standard error, and a `refine run` whose output was lost does not start its program.
D	1062	What an SVD omits, overstates or says twice is refused where it says it	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1062-what-an-svd-omits-overstates-or-says-twice-is-refused-where-it-says-it	Chosen: each is L0529, placed at the element. A child the projection reads as a number and the element lacks is refused naming both, whichever caller reads it: an interrupt's `value`, read for every peripheral of the file whether or not it is selected, and an array's `dimIncrement` were the two unguarded. Each number is bounded before it meets another: a `bitWidth` is 1 to 32 and a `bitOffset` at most 32 less it, an `addressOffset` and a `dimIncrement` are each 32-bit before one is multiplied by an element's position and added to the other and to the base, and `deviceNumInterrupts` is at most 65536, one more than the highest number an interrupt may have. A selected name has one reading: two peripherals of the name a policy selects or a peripheral derives from, two registers of a selected name, and a selected name that is both a register and an element of an array, or an element of two arrays, are refused at the second. A field that gives its position in more than one of the three forms gives the same bits in each. A field has at most two `enumeratedValues`, the one read and the one written that CMSIS-SVD admits; a third is L0528.\n\nThe reader and the projection also take time that grows with the file and not with its square: an element's attributes, a field's enumerated values and a device's interrupts are each looked up in an ordered set, where each was compared with every one before it, and a few hundred kilobytes ran for minutes.

An interrupt that would be a source of that name is L0528, and the policy's `interrupt_corrections` can omit it; as a slot of a core without a matrix its name is a string and is written. A selected peripheral whose lowercased name is reserved is L0528, and a part of the policy's `prefix` that is reserved is L0526, because no import can name either.

D	1074	A program the grammar derives is read by the grammar alone	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1074-a-program-the-grammar-derives-is-read-by-the-grammar-alone	Chosen: a file is read first by the grammar alone. No closer is looked for beforehand: a function is closed by the `end` its body leaves, and a bare block's `end` is its own whatever follows it. When that reading has nothing to report it is the parse, so in a program the grammar derives the place a line begins decides nothing, as [1750] says. When it has anything to report it is given up at that point, having reported nothing, and the file is read again with D260's recovery, which makes every report; a file with a mistake costs at most one more reading up to its first mistake.\n\nThree things change in the recovering reading. A construct that closes with a bare `end` and meets the closer found for its function, in a body that has reported nothing, is reported as never closed, and the closer stays the function's; after a report in the routine it is taken quietly as before, being what that mistake did to the rest of the body. A bare block leaves an `end` for a construct around it only when `end if`, `end match` or `end unchecked` is written on one line and an `if`, `match` or `unchecked` is open around the block. And the bare `end` a function is fenced by is looked for only as far as the first line no deeper than the function: when that line is anything else, what follows is another declaration's, and the function is closed by whichever `end` its body leaves.\n\n`refine fmt` parses what it laid out, and a layout that no longer parses is a compiler defect that leaves the file as it was, beside the one for a changed token.\n\nWhat the grammar derives is accepted as derived even where a person would read the layout otherwise: a routine whose last block lost its `end`, followed at the margin by a function-typed binding and a stray `end`, is one routine with that binding inside it.
D	1075	Removing one of two brackets is a guess	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1075-removing-one-of-two-brackets-is-a-guess	Chosen: the removal of `(`, `)`, `[` or `]` is Likely, however few repairs were found. Exact remains for a token whose second copy cannot be one half of a pair: `x:: u32`, `mut mut`, a closing word written again.
D	1076	The repair search reads a routine for its first refused line alone	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1076-the-repair-search-reads-a-routine-for-its-first-refused-line-alone	Chosen: a line is not tried when the parser reported an error earlier in its routine. D	1077	A bidirectional control in a comment or a literal is warned about	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1077-a-bidirectional-control-in-a-comment-or-a-literal-is-warned-about	Chosen: a comment or a literal holding one of those eleven characters is reported once, at its first, as the warning L0628. D	1084	A view no name holds is in use until what took it is done	Decisions: Lifetime, escape and allocation	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1084-a-view-no-name-holds-is-in-use-until-what-took-it-is-done	Chosen: a view is in use until what it was evaluated for is done with it, whether or not a name holds it.\n\n- The source of a `for` is in use from the loop's head to its last iteration. In the body, passing what it views `inout` or `sink` is L0315 when some path from the call reaches the next iteration, or reads the loop's element where the element names the walked storage in place [1160]. A call the loop leaves straight after, by `break`, `return` or a failure, is accepted, and so is one in `complete`, which runs when the walk is over.\n- An argument is in use until its call returns. What it views is not passed `inout` or `sink` to the same call, in either order and whether the view is written in the call or held by a name whose last use the call is; nor to a call nested in a later argument, since arguments are evaluated left to right [0410]. A reference only read out of a field of a binding has other storage under it and holds nothing, so a record is passed `inout` to an entry of an `any` the record holds. An address or a range of one field holds no other field of the same binding, where both are reached by fields alone.\n\n[0830]'s rule for a view a name holds is unchanged, and still counts a reference read out of a field when the name is read after the call.\n\nA result whose `from` names a container is a view of the container even when what it returns is a reference the container only stored, as `vec.get` of a list of pointers returns: the signature says so and the caller is held to it.

D	1110	On Xtensa a routine's outgoing area is part of its frame	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1110-on-xtensa-a-routine-s-outgoing-area-is-part-of-its-frame	Chosen: the stack pointer does not move after the prologue. A routine's outgoing area, the largest any of its calls takes, sixteen-byte aligned, is the lowest bytes of its frame: the prologue reserves it with the word homes and the source homes, sets the base of the homes above it, and checks the whole against the stack's limit where a program prepares stacks (D471), so a call's area has no check of its own. That is no instruction more on arm64, one on RISC-V, Xtensa and Cortex-M and two on x86-64. A program that prepares no stack still has no check, and its code is what it was.

A list of bytes grows through `mem.reserve_admit_copy`, D356's protocol with the copy of the appended bytes made before a moved block is released. A growing builder grows the same way when the old block may be read again, in place through the allocator's `grow` and otherwise into a fresh block, appending before it frees the old one. That is when the appended bytes lie in the block, which their addresses say while it is live, and when a `format` is writing: `text.format` writes several values and a template, any of which may view the builder, so while a `format` writes, the builder keeps the first block a growth moves it out of and the call frees it when it ends; a `format` a conformance calls inside another keeps its own, and hands it to the outer call when that one has kept none. Every other growth still calls the allocator's `resize`, as D425 measured it: nothing reads the old block again, and `hosted/heap` moves a large block's pages instead of copying them. The promise is the call's own: a view of the old block is still invalid once the call has returned, and a routine of the program's that appends twice from a view it holds behind a pointer is not made safe by it. Whether the checker refuses the direct spellings is the origin check's rule and changes nothing here: the library is sound with them accepted and with them refused.

This reverses D1045's declined alternative for these descriptors: standard output and standard error that are a terminal are refused, and so is a blocking device such as `/dev/null`, whose kind promises nothing. D	1280	A signal handler is installed as a C function value, through a second view of `sigaction`'s record	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1280-a-signal-handler-is-installed-as-a-c-function-value-through-a-second-view-of-sigaction-s-record	Chosen: `libc.signal_handler` is the handler's type, `extern(c) (number: i32) -> none`. That retyping is the library's and is sound for the reason C's own member is a union of a function and a word: both records are one C layout, and an `extern(c)` function value in a record C reads is the function's address [1975]. `signal_action` and `sigaction` are unchanged, so a disposition that is no function, and every read of a previous action, stay words. The handler stays `platform/libc`'s: on a static Linux program nothing installs one, since x86-64's `rt_sigaction` needs a restorer the library cannot write, and `signal.watch` reads signals without any.
D	1281	A program that reads the argument root before it exists is told the call it lacks	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1281-a-program-that-reads-the-argument-root-before-it-exists-is-told-the-call-it-lacks	Chosen: before that trap `platform/posix` writes one line to standard error: `landin: the host was not initialized: a C main calls _landin_host_initialize_arguments(argc, argv, envp) first`. The write is the system's own to descriptor 2 and asks nothing of the root; when it fails the trap still follows. The trap, its kind and what a panic handler sees are unchanged, and the other misuses of the root, a second triple or a negative count, stay bare traps.
D	1290	An RV32 slot whose routine is out of a jump's reach enters it through a stub	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1290-an-rv32-slot-whose-routine-is-out-of-a-jump-s-reach-enters-it-through-a-stub	Chosen: such a slot is `j _landin_firmware_far_N`, a stub in `.text.landin_firmware_trap` beside the table, and the stub reaches anywhere with `auipc` and `jr`. Which slots get one is read from the profile and not from the link: slot N is far when its routine's region is not the text's and some byte of that region lies more than 1 MiB from the table. A routine in the text, and one in a region wholly in reach, is jumped to as before, so an image none of whose routines is far is byte for byte the image it was.\n\nThe pair needs a register for the address, and what it may take depends on who enters the slot:\n\n- A slot the core's dispatch calls (`clic`'s common entry, `xh3irq`'s external entry) is called with t0 holding the slot's own address, after the entry saved the interrupted registers, and a call may change t0. Its stub is `auipc t0` and `jr` to the routine, eight bytes.\n- A slot the hardware enters has every register the interrupted code's, and a naked routine there is promised them. Its stub lowers sp by 16, stores t0 at 0(sp), and jumps with `auipc t0` and `jr` to a landing, `_landin_firmware_far_N_landing`, linked in the routine's own section family and so beside it; the landing reloads t0, raises sp by 16 and is one `j` to the routine. The routine is entered with all thirty-one registers and mepc as the hardware left them. Sixteen bytes below the interrupted sp are written, as an interrupt routine's own stub writes the bytes below it (D680), and a naked routine that may not assume the interrupted stack, which no RISC-V core without a separate interrupt stack lets it avoid, has none of its own to use either.\n\nAn interrupt routine in a hardware-entered slot is entered by its stub `_landin_firmware_slot_N`, which is in the text, takes the routine's address with `auipc` and `addi` after saving t0 and calls it through a register; it was never the slot's jump and is unchanged. The entry word jumps to reset or to the stage, both in the text, and is unchanged. With debugging information both the stub and the landing carry unwind rules that return to mepc and find t0 in its slot.
D	1291	`--debug=lines` names each module binding, with its type	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1291-debug-lines-names-each-module-binding-with-its-type	Chosen: `--debug=lines` describes each module datum a declaration names, as a variable of the compilation unit: its source name, its declaration's file, line and column, its type, and the one address expression `DW_OP_addr SYMBOL`, the symbol being whatever D415 and D417 linked it as. Its type is described as `--debug=full` describes one, by the same encoder: scalars, pointers, structs with their fields, arrays, and D423's enumeration for an atom-set value. A debugger resolves a bare name in an expression to the variable before a routine of that name, so `print geometry` is the binding's value, `ptype geometry` its type and `&geometry` its address, and `break geometry` is still the routine. No link name changes, and nothing is added to a loaded segment.\n\n`lines` still describes no routine's parameters, locals or slots and emits no location list: those need the placement plan `--debug=full` reads, which no firmware backend offers. A unit with no module binding has the debugging sections it had, byte for byte. Hosted targets refuse `lines` and already describe module data under `full`; they are unchanged.
D	1292	`refine site` resolves a site, or a caller's coordinates, against its build	Decisions: Functions, calls and returns	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1292-refine-site-resolves-a-site-or-a-caller-s-coordinates-against-its-build	Chosen: `refine site [--map=FILE] [--dsym=FILE] PROGRAM SITE` and `refine site ... PROGRAM FILE LINE COLUMN`. PROGRAM is what the compilation wrote: an executable, a firmware image, or the assembly of `--emit=asm`. The table is `PROGRAM.sources.json` unless `--map` names it. SITE is a `u32` in decimal or after `0x`. The answer on standard output is the recorded path's bytes, `:LINE:COLUMN`, and for a site the check that failed in parentheses, as the script wrote them, and the status is 0.\n\nThe table answers only for the build it was written with, and the command reads that build's identity itself rather than being told it: an ELF's `.landin_id` section, which every firmware image carries, or else its GNU build ID, which a hosted link is given and `strip` keeps; a thin arm64 Mach-O's `__TEXT,__landin_id` section, and with `--dsym` the dSYM's DWARF file must share the executable's UUID; anything else is read as assembly, whose SHA-256 must be the table's `assembly_sha256`. A table that is not one is L0688, a build that is not the table's L0689, and a site, a file number or an operand the table does not hold L0690, each with status 1; a file that cannot be read is L0003. Site 0 is the compiler's own guard and is refused by name. Every file is read through `Landin.Platform`, nothing is written and no tool is run.\n\n"The built program's debug information" is this table and not DWARF: a site is defined by D232 as a source byte and a check family, the table is the one artifact that records it on every target, firmware and a stripped executable included, and DWARF line tables name instructions, not sites. The script is removed; the debugger lanes and the Cortex-M panic control call the command.
D	1293	A handler reports its verdict by resuming `main`	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1293-a-handler-reports-its-verdict-by-resuming-main	Chosen: D462's resume is the portable report and no mechanism is added. D450 admits the stack builtins on every target with a native backend and every backend now emits them, RV32 and Xtensa included, so the one source runs on every hosted lane and every firmware corpus. A fixture that pins a handler runs the computation whose check fails on a prepared stack; the handler stores its verdict in a module value and resumes the context `main` saved when it switched there, and `main` returns the verdict as its `status`, which a hosted lane reads as the process's and a firmware harness as the value `main` returned. The verdict is 42 for exactly the expected kind and site and a distinct code otherwise, so a missing dispatch, another kind, another site and a call that returned each fail the status. The handler does not return, so D232's rule for a returning handler is not engaged, and its latch stays claimed as D462 says. A check that fails on `main`'s own stack, before any switch, has no saved context to resume; a fixture of one keeps `traps: yes`.
D	1306	A recorded report holds a library line by its text, not its number	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1306-a-recorded-report-holds-a-library-line-by-its-text-not-its-number	Chosen: the harness records and compares a report in its recorded form. A location in a file outside the fixture's own directory, read lexically from where refine ran, keeps its file, its column, the line it quotes and its carets, and its line number is written `*`, in the location and in the quoted line's gutter, whose width becomes the marker's; a location in the fixture's own files and every other byte stay as refine printed them. A moved library line therefore leaves every recording as it was, and a changed one, or a span that moved within its line, fails each fixture that quotes it. The test program's two recording commands write that form, its recorded cases and Darwin's diagnostics lane compare it, and a full `check.py` refuses a recording that still numbers a library line. A library is what lies outside the fixture: `core`, `hosted`, `platform` and a device description alike.
D	1307	The scripts say when a refine is not its checkout's	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1307-the-scripts-say-when-a-refine-is-not-its-checkout-s	Chosen: `scripts/refine_revision.py` asks a binary `refine version --json` and compares its source digest, the digest of the compiler sources it was built from, with the checkout's (`scripts/build_identity.py`). The digest decides: equal is current, whatever the revision or dirtiness say, so a build made before a commit of documents is not stale. Otherwise one warning line says how it parts, by its revision: older, an ancestor of HEAD, with the commits between counted, or HEAD itself built from a clean tree that has uncommitted edits to compiler sources since; HEAD built from a dirty tree, whose edits are not the tree's now; newer, a descendant of HEAD; another line of history, a commit neither contains, or one the checkout lacks; and a build outside git. A program that does not answer as refine does is not judged. `dev-build.sh` and `dev-test.sh` ask after their build and every lane that takes `--refine` asks after reading its arguments; the warning never changes a status.

D	1317	A library documentation comment is at most 79 columns	Decisions: The core library and the derived programs	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1317-a-library-documentation-comment-is-at-most-79-columns	Chosen: a `---` documentation comment line in `core`, `hosted` or `platform` is at most 79 columns, counted in characters with its indentation and its marker, the width the compiler's own Ada sources keep; a full `check.py` refuses a longer one, naming the line, and the twelve were rewrapped within their paragraphs. `docs/format.md` says that the layout itself holds a comment to no width and a program's comments are its own. D	1320	An ordinary RISC-V block's text names x0 to read and to write	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1320-an-ordinary-risc-v-block-s-text-names-x0-to-read-and-to-write	Chosen: an ordinary block's text on RV64 and RV32 may name `x0` or `zero` as a source and as a destination. x0 reads as zero and discards writes, so naming it overwrites nothing the routine keeps and cannot break the register-allocation contract an ordinary block's other rules protect: the compiler neither saves it nor chooses it for `general`. An operand still never names it, to read or to write: an `in` operand at x0 would lose its value and an `out` would always read zero, so `in v: u32 at x0` stays L0330, whose note now says why and that the text names `zero` itself. The scratch-register and `csrw` notes are gone. A naked body named x0 before and still does.
D	1321	An array length reads a compiler fact and `sizeof` of a scalar	Decisions: Arrays, slices and text	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1321-an-array-length-reads-a-compiler-fact-and-sizeof-of-a-scalar	Chosen: an array length, wherever its type is written, a routine body, a signature, a struct field and an alias template included, may read an integer compiler fact (`compiler.word_size`, `compiler.cache_line`) and `sizeof` of a built-in scalar type, directly, and so may the image of a module integer D438 counts. Each folds as the literal it stands for: the fact is the value configuration found for the selected target once it chose the arms, and the size is that target's storage size of the scalar, so a 32-bit target's `[sizeof usize]u8` is `[4]u8` on a 64-bit host. Both are known before checking begins, exactly as the selected arm of a `fixed if` is, and type identity has depended on the target since D139. A bool fact in a length is refused as no count, an atom fact alone stays L0203, and every other measurement, `sizeof` of a declared type, a fixed array or a type formal, and `alignof` of anything, stays L0305 with a message that says what folds. A fixed actual of a type application is still an integer literal or a forwarded fixed formal (D135), and a routine body still reads no fact as a value.
D	1322	Every instance of a placed generic routine goes to its placement	Decisions: The toolchain, C and the machine	https://www.701.dev/spec.html#d1322-every-instance-of-a-placed-generic-routine-goes-to-its-placement	Chosen: on a firmware target, `link(section: ...)`, `link(align: ...)` and `link(region: ...)` on a generic routine place every instance of it: each instance the program makes is emitted in that section, at that alignment or in that region, as a nongeneric routine placed there would be, under its own instance name. The instances are made by calls, so a placed generic routine is no root of its own and one nothing calls places nothing. `link(vector: ...)` and `link(boot_stage)` name the one routine a slot or the boot kind enters, and `keep` retains a routine no call reaches, so a generic routine takes none of them: L0347, naming the generic parameter and the nongeneric routine that calls it. A hosted target places nothing, a generic routine included, as before. The build and stack reports list each instance as they list an unplaced one. An evidence adapter the compiler makes for an instance that is itself a conformance's provider is not an instance and is not placed.
